name: python-memory-guardian
description: Static + runtime analysis for CPython: flags heap inflation, RAM fragmentation, text inflation, memory swell and single-threaded stalls as you type, and measures per-line time (Python / native / system) and memory with a built-in low-overhead profiler.

pythonMemoryGuardian.backend.description: Language server implementation. Both apply identical rules and messages.

pythonMemoryGuardian.interpreter.description: Interpreter your code runs on. It is probed at startup (object sizes, GIL state, allocator) so diagnostics quote numbers for that exact Python; the Python backend also runs on it (3.9+). Empty = python3/python on PATH.

enumDescriptions: Sampled time and process RSS observations; no allocating-line attribution
tracemalloc: live traced block paths and recent retention candidates; substantial allocation-dependent overhead
pythonMemoryGuardian.profile.memoryMode.description: Default memory mode shown first when profiling.

pythonMemoryGuardian.profile.hotShare.description: A line using at least this fraction of runtime is 'hot': its static diagnostics are raised one severity level.

pythonMemoryGuardian.profile.hotMB.description: A line allocating at least this many MB is 'hot'.

pythonMemoryGuardian.container.execPrefi.markdownDescription: **Only for plain Docker/Compose with the editor on the host.** Command prefix that runs a program inside your container, e.g. `["docker", "compose", "exec", "-T", "app"]`. When set, the interpreter probe and the profiler run inside the container. Leave empty for Dev Containers, Codespaces, WSL and Remote-SSH.

pythonMemoryGuardian.container.interpret.description: Python executable inside the container (container mode only).

pythonMemoryGuardian.container.pathMappi.markdownDescription: Host ↔ container path pairs for container mode, e.g. `[{"local": "${workspaceFolder}", "container": "/app"}]` (the folder your compose file bind-mounts).

pythonMemoryGuardian.trace.server.description: Log LSP traffic between VS Code and the language server to the 'Python Memory Guardian' output channel.

pythonMemoryGuardian.profile.frames.markdownDescription: Precise mode: traceback depth `tracemalloc` records per allocation. Higher values tie more memory allocated inside libraries back to your lines, but slow profiling (measured on `import pandas`: 2 frames 1.3 s, 8 frames 2.9 s, 32 frames 7.5 s).

pythonMemoryGuardian.profile.monitoring.description: Optional Python 3.12+ execution-event coverage. Counts user-line events; sampled timing and memory measurements are unchanged. Can increase overhead.

pythonMemoryGuardian.profile.allocationB.description: Optional allocator request capture. Memray must be installed in the target interpreter; requests are distinct from objects and RSS.

pythonMemoryGuardian.profile.diagnostics.description: Capture cooperative workload and access evidence through pmg_diagnostics and save a JSONL trace.

pythonMemoryGuardian.profile.memoryGuard.description: Supervise the profiled process externally and stop on a measured RSS budget or low system headroom. Polling can overshoot; Linux also applies a virtual-address-space limit.

pythonMemoryGuardian.profile.memoryLimit.description: Optional smaller profiling-process memory budget in MiB. Zero uses 25% of initially available memory, subject to the system reserve. Includes in-process profiler memory.

pythonMemoryGuardian.profile.memoryReser.description: System memory reserve in MiB, bounded to half initially available memory. Profiling stops when available memory reaches this reserve.

pythonMemoryGuardian.profile.allocationD.description: Full captures Python and system allocator requests. System omits individual Python allocator requests to reduce capture cost; object/allocation coverage is lost.
